aknow: Earlier form of Acknow. (old) To be aknow, to acknowledge; to confess. (old)
akimbo: With a crook or bend; with the hand on the hip and elbow turned outward. "With one arm akimbo." Irving.
akin: 1. Of the same kin; related by blood; -- used of persons; as, the two families are near akin. 2. Allied by nature; partaking of the same properties; of the same kind. "A joy akin to rapture." Cowper. The literary character of the work is akin to its moral character. Jeffrey. Note: This adjective is used only after the noun.
akinesia: Paralysis of the motor nerves; loss of movement. Foster.
